expected: Disposal.fees should reflect the fee actually charged on the sale. app/core/lots.py's Disposal.gain_loss property is `proceeds - fees - cost_basis` and clearly designed to net a fee -- but it reads fees only from the SELL transaction's own `.fees` field (`per_share_fees = txn.fees / qty`), never looking up a standalone FEE-action row tied to the same sale. Robinhood and SoFi's real exports carry standalone FEE/EMRF/transfer-fee rows too (already established by the confirmed cash-settled-unsettled-split-fee-misattributed fix), so this is not a harness-only artifact.

My own fill record and the paper broker's settled_cash agree the net economic result was $675.15, a $1.42 loss. /tax and GET /api/tax/report both report proceeds=675.17, cost_basis=676.57, fees=0.00, gain_loss=-1.40, fees_unknown=false, disallowed_loss=0.00 -- Form 8949's Adjustment column is also $0.00. title: Realised gain/loss ignores a sale's standalone FEE ledger row, understating every loss by the fee

verification.note: The code gap is real: `Disposal.fees` is taken from the SELL row's own `fees` column, so a standalone FEE row is never attributed to the disposal it belongs to. The measured impact is not. Every standalone fee row in the real ledger is account-level -- two Gold subscription fees, three ACAT-out fees, an early IRA-match removal fee, one SoFi brokerage fee -- none carrying a symbol or instrument, and none of them a selling cost. Reducing proceeds by them would be wrong. 0 of 926 real sell rows carry any fee at all, which is why the app already warns FEES_UNKNOWN on 547 rows rather than claiming fees are zero. The $0.02 the persona measured is real in the harness, which deliberately writes per-trade regulatory fees as their own rows. Left unfixed on purpose: attributing standalone fee rows to disposals needs a link these rows do not carry, and guessing would charge a $448.56 IRA-match-removal fee against an unrelated sale.

why_it_matters: Form 8949 is the document filed with the IRS. A gain/loss column that silently drops SEC/TAF fees understates every loss (or overstates every gain) that has a standalone fee row, by exactly the fee each time -- small per trade, systematic across a real ledger with hundreds of sales, and it is asserted as certain (fees_unknown=false) rather than flagged.
